description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between TriviaQA initial confidence and three distinct accuracy metrics. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence", displays a sequence of explicitly labeled, non-uniformly spaced numeric tick values ranging from 0.71 to 1.00, with labels including 0.71, 0.73, 0.79, 0.82 through 0.87, and continuous increments from 0.90 to 1.00 rotated at an angle. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy", uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks regularly spaced at intervals of 0.2. All three lines include vertical error bars at each data point plotted over a dashed background grid. The "Final Accuracy" metric is represented by a solid blue line with black-edged circular markers; it begins at approximately 0.91 at x=0.71, drops to its lowest point of roughly 0.72 at x=0.73, achieves peaks of 1.0 at x=0.79, 0.92, and 0.96, and ends at approximately 0.98 at x=1.00. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" metric is depicted by a dashed orange line with black-edged diamond markers, starting at roughly 0.36 at x=0.71, dipping to a minimum of approximately 0.04 at x=0.90, displaying prominent peaks of about 0.46 at x=0.87 and x=0.94, and concluding at approximately 0.08 at x=1.00. Finally, the "Initial Accuracy" is shown as a dash-dot green line with black-edged square markers, commencing at approximately 0.55 at x=0.71, rising to an early high of 0.92 at x=0.79, experiencing sharp declines to approximately 0.46 at both x=0.87 and x=0.94, and finishing at roughly 0.90 at x=1.00.
